title: TN HB0545: AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, relative to artificial intelligence.

obligations: The department shall provide at least one professional development course for teachers that provides asynchronous instruction on the use of artificial intelligence in the classroom, made available at no cost to teachers in grades six through twelve, and that may be used to earn professional development points (Sec. 1(a)).
The course content must be created by an entity with experience in a related subject area, such as computer science or another science, technology, engineering, and mathematics field (Sec. 1(a)).

Teachers in grades six through twelve must complete at least one professional development course approved by the department that provides asynchronous instruction on the use of artificial intelligence in the classroom by August 1, 2028, or within two years of becoming licensed as a teacher in this state, whichever is later (Sec. 1(b)).

Each LEA and public charter school shall approve professional development points, pursuant to the state board of education's educator licensure policies and rules, for a teacher's completion of at least one department approved artificial intelligence training (Sec. 1(b)).

What it does

This law requires the Tennessee department of education to provide at least one free asynchronous professional development course on using artificial intelligence in the classroom for teachers in grades six through twelve. It also requires those teachers to complete at least one department approved artificial intelligence course by August 1, 2028 or within two years of becoming licensed, whichever is later. Each LEA and public charter school must approve professional development points for completion of that training.

Who it applies to

  • Tennessee department of education
  • teachers in grades six through twelve
  • LEAs
  • public charter schools

Effective date

upon becoming a law

Key definitions

  • not stated in the text

Obligations

  • The department shall provide at least one professional development course for teachers that provides asynchronous instruction on the use of artificial intelligence in the classroom, made available at no cost to teachers in grades six through twelve, and that may be used to earn professional development points (Sec. 1(a)).
  • The course content must be created by an entity with experience in a related subject area, such as computer science or another science, technology, engineering, and mathematics field (Sec. 1(a)).
  • Teachers in grades six through twelve must complete at least one professional development course approved by the department that provides asynchronous instruction on the use of artificial intelligence in the classroom by August 1, 2028, or within two years of becoming licensed as a teacher in this state, whichever is later (Sec. 1(b)).
  • Each LEA and public charter school shall approve professional development points, pursuant to the state board of education's educator licensure policies and rules, for a teacher's completion of at least one department approved artificial intelligence training (Sec. 1(b)).

Prohibitions

  • not stated in the text

Penalties and enforcement

not stated in the text

How it affects AI deployment

  • The law does not directly regulate artificial intelligence deployment; it imposes training and approval duties on the department, LEAs, public charter schools, and teachers (Sec. 1).
  • An LEA or public charter school must approve professional development points for a teacher's completion of at least one department approved artificial intelligence training (Sec. 1(b)).
  • A teacher in grades six through twelve must complete the required artificial intelligence course by the deadline (Sec. 1(b)).
  • The department must provide the course at no cost to teachers in grades six through twelve (Sec. 1(a)).

Notable exemptions

  • not stated in the text

Compliance steps

  • The department must create or procure at least one asynchronous artificial intelligence professional development course for grades six through twelve teachers, with content created by an entity with experience in computer science or another STEM field, and make it available at no cost (Sec. 1(a)).
  • LEAs and public charter schools must identify teachers in grades six through twelve and ensure they complete at least one department approved artificial intelligence course by August 1, 2028 or within two years of licensure, whichever is later (Sec. 1(b)).
  • LEAs and public charter schools must approve professional development points for a teacher's completion of at least one department approved artificial intelligence training, pursuant to state board of education licensure policies and rules (Sec. 1(b)).
  • Teachers in grades six through twelve must complete the required course by the deadline (Sec. 1(b)).

 By Cochran, Cepicky, Hardaway

AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, relative to artificial intelligence.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 49, Chapter 1, Part 2, is amended by adding
the following as a new section:

 (a) The department shall provide at least one (1) professional development course for
 teachers that provides asynchronous instruction on the use of artificial intelligence in the
 classroom; that is made available, at no cost, to teachers in grades six through twelve (6-12);
 and that may be used by teachers to earn professional development points. The course
 content must be created by an entity with experience in a related subject area, such as
 computer science or another science, technology, engineering, and mathematics {STEM)
 field.

 (b) By August 1, 2028, or within two (2) years of becoming licensed as a teacher in
 this state, whichever is later, teachers in grades six through twelve (6-12) must complete at
 least one ( 1) professional development course approved by the department that provides
 asynchronous instruction on the use of artificial intelligence in the classroom. Each LEA and
 public charter school shall approve professional development points, pursuant to the state
 board of education's educator licensure policies and rules, for a teacher's completion of at
 least one (1) department-approved artificial intelligence training.

 SECTION 2. This act takes effect upon becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it.
  SENATE BILL NO. 677
